title: Product Photography Studio Simulator
description: The user operates a virtual photography studio where they position a shoe on a turntable and an antique camera on a tripod. They adjust lighting rigs, swap shoe material variants, rotate the turntable, aim the camera, and capture snapshots to a gallery strip. An energy budget conserves total light intensity across three colored spotlights, and full undo/redo tracks every action.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements a product photography studio. Load MaterialsVariantsShoe.glb centered on a circular turntable platform (a short cylinder) at world origin. Load AntiqueCamera.glb on a tripod-like stand positioned 3 units away, facing the shoe. Use GLTFLoader for both models. Scene setup: a dark studio environment with a ground plane, subtle ambient light (intensity 0.15), and THREE colored SpotLights (red, green, blue) mounted on visible pole meshes above the turntable. The three spotlights share a conserved total intensity budget of 3.0; adjusting one via its slider redistributes intensity proportionally from the others so the sum always equals 3.0. UI panel (HTML overlay, top-left): three range sliders for spotlight intensities (0.0-2.5 each, enforcing conservation), a dropdown to switch the shoe's material variant using KHR_materials_variants, a turntable rotation slider (0-360 degrees rotating the shoe platform), camera-aim horizontal angle slider (-30 to 30 degrees rotating the AntiqueCamera model around Y), a Capture button that renders the current viewport to a 128px thumbnail appended to a bottom gallery strip (max 5, oldest removed), and Undo/Redo buttons. Implement an action history stack: every slider release, variant change, or capture pushes a state snapshot (all slider values, variant index, gallery thumbnails as data URLs). Undo restores the previous snapshot and re-applies all values; Redo re-applies forward. The viewer camera uses OrbitControls targeting midpoint between shoe and antique camera. Add a subtle environment map (PMREMGenerator with a RoomEnvironment or simple gradient) for realistic reflections on the shoe. Ensure at least 10-14 meaningful interaction steps are possible: adjust 3 lights, rotate turntable, aim camera, switch 2+ material variants, capture 2+ photos, undo, redo. Display a step counter in the UI showing total actions performed.
